scope: k=2 weak metric dimension of K_n square K_m; supporting evidence for K2_RESOLUTION.md. Computational agreement is evidence, not proof.

methods.exact_enum: independent weighted pair-witness subset enumeration (src/exact_hittingset.py); proves both directions on the listed small instances
methods.ilp: HiGHS branch-and-bound on the full pair-constraint formulation (scripts/certify_k2_ilp.py, scipy); every returned set re-validated against the original distance definition
methods.direct_set_check: explicit transversal sets verified by two independent code paths (src/weak_k_metric.py and an independent scratch reimplementation)

exact_enum_certified.note: m = 2n-3; formula wdim_2 = m fails, matches Theorem 1.1 value ceil(4n/3) = 4
m = 2n-3; fails strictly; consistent with Table 1 of the paper (8)

threshold_observation.statement: wdim_2 = m iff m >= 2n-2 in every computed instance (n = 3..7); below the seam the values match ceil(2(n+m)/3)
threshold_observation.proved: K2_RESOLUTION.md proves both directions for all n >= 3: wdim_2 = m for m >= 2n-2 (Lemmas 1+4), and wdim_2 >= m+1 for 3 <= m <= 2n-3 (Lemmas 2+3+5)
threshold_observation.sub_threshold_conjecture_unproved: wdim_2 = ceil(2(n+m)/3) for n <= m <= 2n-3 fits all exact data and contains the square case ceil(4n/3) of Theorem 1.1; no proof claimed

paper_discrepancy.claim_checked: Fernandez et al., Concluding remarks: 'when n = 5, the formula does not hold for m in {6,...,9}, and for n = 6 ... m in {7,...,11}'; Table 1 (n=5) k=2 row reports m=8 -> 9 and m=9 -> 10
paper_discrepancy.finding: the formula HOLDS at m = 2n-2 and m = 2n-1: exact ILP gives wdim_2(K_5[]K_8) = 8, wdim_2(K_5[]K_9) = 9, wdim_2(K_6[]K_10) = 10, wdim_2(K_6[]K_11) = 11, and explicit directly-verified transversal sets of size m exist (see below). For n=6 the remark even contradicts the paper's own Table 2, which reports 10 and 11. The Table 1 k=2 entries for m in {8,9} appear to be overestimates from the paper's modified ILP formulation for k in {2,3}.

diagonal_failure_at_2n_minus_1.statement: the plain diagonal f(j) = j mod n is NOT weak 2-resolving at m = 2n-1 (row sums (2,...,2,1); a swap pair through the degree-1 row has Delta = 1)
